findings.Quote: He'd come into the world with a sword that had no history, and not much of one himself.

findings.Quote: Warm and strange at odd hours of the night.

findings.Quote: Pencil meant it might still get resolved. Ink meant settled.
findings.Note: A tidy aphoristic rule stated as if universal, slightly precious and unearned as a metaphysical claim about pencil vs ink.

findings.Quote: She watched him eat it with the satisfaction of a person who'd solved a small logistics problem.
findings.Note: Cleverness-forward simile that tells rather than shows her characterization, slightly undercutting the more effective 'reading him' beat that follows.

findings.Quote: They breathed: a slow pressure-release hiss that sounded mechanical and just slightly not.

findings.Quote: "All good engineering is anticlimactic." She headed for the door. "If it's interesting, something went wrong."
findings.Note: Reads as a tacked-on aphorism/quip rather than character speech, slightly undercutting the wordless-competence purpose with an explanatory truism.
findings.Fix: Cut the second line or replace with an action beat that shows rather than states the philosophy.

findings.Quote: Pixel went quiet. The high-resolution kind.
findings.Note: Cute abstract descriptor tells rather than shows her reaction; undercuts the escalating dread of the reveal.
findings.Fix: Show a concrete physical tell instead.

findings.Quote: Under all of it was something older: old wood, maybe, or just the warmth a room holds after cooking for years.
findings.Note: Hedging vague description ('maybe') reads as filler atmosphere rather than grounded detail, weakening the otherwise precise establishing prose.
findings.Fix: Cut the hedge; commit to one concrete image, e.g. 'Under it was old wood, decades of grease worked into the grain.'

findings.Quote: Get through the assessment, learn what she actually wanted, and walk out on his own feet — that was the whole of it.
findings.Note: Explicit statement of internal goal tells the reader what to feel about the scene instead of letting the action carry it; borders on stock resolve-summary phrasing.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold into action/dialogue rather than stating it as narrated intention.

findings.Quote: He knew what it cost her.
findings.Note: Generic telling-not-showing emotional shorthand that states the theme directly instead of trusting the preceding concrete details.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let the itemized details (hinge, tracking, held data) carry the cost.

findings.Quote: Vey had told him once that provenance wasn't about whether a thing was real. It was about chain of custody. You couldn't prove a thing was genuine. You could only know who had held it, in what order, and whether the hands made sense.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound aphorism block spelling out the chapter's title/theme explicitly, which reads as authorial explanation rather than earned character reflection.
findings.Fix: Trim to a single line or cut; let the freight-tag image already do the thematic work.

findings.Quote: She looked at him the way you check a sample against the paperwork.

findings.Fix: Vary the comparison or cut, since the 'exact' characterization was already delivered via her bow in ref 0 and her reading-a-page look in ref 2.

findings.Quote: the loneliest steel he'd handled, and meant it

findings.Quote: An oversight, maybe. A deliberate falsification, also maybe. For Tessaline's legal exposure it wouldn't matter, and that was the part that did.

findings.Quote: Together they were the work of someone sure no one would look.

findings.Quote: Clean on a schedule, not clean because someone had noticed it was dirty.
findings.Note: Overwritten aphoristic distinction that tells rather than shows, slightly precious for a scene-setting detail.

findings.Quote: He had the face of a man who assumed he was the most important person in any room.
findings.Note: Stock character-summary phrasing, a familiar type-cliché for corporate antagonists.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical tell instead of a generalized assumption-about-himself line.

findings.Quote: Kyle waited. He was good at waiting.
findings.Note: Tells the reader a trait rather than demonstrating it beyond what's already shown; slightly redundant aphoristic beat.

findings.Quote: The knot in his stomach eased.
findings.Note: First interior emotional admission in the scene undercuts the otherwise controlled, external POV that has carried the confrontation; slight tonal shift toward telling.

findings.Quote: the way she did when she had more to say and hadn't decided whether to say it

findings.Quote: The corner as it was now, and what it could have been.

findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with something concrete: "He'd half-known it for a while. Not afraid of it. Just aware."

findings.Quote: His jaw set without his deciding it, back teeth pressed together hard enough to feel.

findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a more specific, non-generic physical beat unique to Kyle.

findings.Quote: Eleven years someone had been reading him like a chart, and he'd never felt the pen.
findings.Note: Mixed metaphor — reading a chart and feeling a pen are two different sensory/metaphor registers spliced together; doesn't survive literal scrutiny (charts are read, pens write — the image conflates being read with being written on).
findings.Fix: Pick one: "Eleven years someone had been reading him like a chart, and he'd never felt the eyes on it."
